items.title: 52150_Charlie Barnet oral history interview
items.q: I think about the only bands that anybody had ever heard of were the Burnett Band, Earl Burnett, and he was at the Biltmore

ctx.x: Well, actually, this saxophone player, a guy by the name of Ralph Spangler, he was there with me, and we kind of joined up with another guy by the name of Tim Lanfier, who was also a saxophone player, and we had like a saxophone section. And I can't tell you the names of anybody we played with there because we were never with anybody that long, because we were totally unruly and we would join the band as a section and we would leave as a section. If anybody said boo to one of us all three of us would leave. And we

played around with, oh, just the local bands there. I couldn't tell you the name of one of them, at that time in California. I think about the only bands that anybody had ever heard of were the Burnett Band, Earl Burnett, and he was at the Biltmore, and then there was the Gus Arnheim Orchestra. Then maybe up in San Francisco there was a band up there. I can't think of his name at the moment, but Phil Harris, he didn't even -- he was still the Loughner Lofner Harris Orchestra.
